maps.for: Keeping exact facts intact through a long conversation
maps.ask: What is losing the facts: the summary, the tool output, or where they sit?
maps.when: Numbers, promises or findings drift or blur as a conversation or multi-step run gets long.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Errors begin well before the window fills
Lost in the middle plus noisy tool output
Case-facts block at the top and trimmed tool results
Tool results carry many unused fields (40 returned, 5 used) and dominate the context
Trim results to the relevant fields before they enter history (for example in a PostToolUse hook)
Exact amounts and promises blur after summarisation (an amount becomes “declined”)
Progressive summarisation: the facts sit inside the history being rewritten
Persistent case-facts block with exact values, carried in every request outside the summary
Facts are present but ignored, buried mid-context
Put key facts first, under a clear heading
An old session is resumed, full of outdated tool results
New session seeded with a structured summary
All the facts already live in a system of record
All prior findings fit in the next agent's input
Nothing is lost if passed whole
Pass the complete prior findings in the prompt
Verbose exploration in a coding session, or findings that must survive a crash or restart
Context pollution, or the context is volatile
Subagent for the exploration; scratchpad or manifest file for the findings
maps.rule: Fix what fills the context before protecting facts from it: trim tool output to the fields you use. Keep numbers and promises in a case-facts block at the top of every request, and don't trust summaries with them.

maps.for: Getting the middle of a long input read
maps.ask: Where do the missed details sit, and is the input already structured?
maps.when: The model follows the start and end of a long document or prompt but misses things in the middle.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Start and end followed, middle missed; input fits, is lean, and only a few key facts matter
Lost in the middle, no structure
Key summary or digest first, plus explicit section headings
Headings already there, middle still lags
Segment it: one request per part
Many detailed items lost mid-input, or the input is too large or has naturally separate parts
Split into shorter passes, then merge the results
Input full of irrelevant fields; tool output buries key facts
Trim to the relevant fields; case-facts block
Numbers, dates and details blur after summarising a long chat
Keep exact facts in a fixed, persistent case-facts block
Mixed document types in one prompt
Output cut off at the end
maps.rule: Strong start and end with a weak middle is a position problem: put key points first under clear section headings. If headings are already there, or there is lots of detail, split the input so nothing sits in the middle.

maps.for: When the agent should hand over to a person
maps.ask: Which escalation trigger is actually present?
maps.when: You must decide whether the agent resolves a customer's issue itself or escalates it to a human.
head: Situation
Agent should
Why
rows: Escalate immediately, with a handoff summary
An explicit demand is a trigger
Customer frustrated or angry but hasn't asked; issue is simple and in scope
Acknowledge and offer the fix; escalate if they then ask again
Policy is silent or needs an exception
Escalation driven by sentiment or self-rated confidence
maps.rule: Escalate on categories: an explicit request for a person (at once, with the facts), a policy gap, or no progress. Frustration alone means offer resolution first; tone and self-rated confidence are not triggers.

maps.for: Fixing an escalation boundary that misfires
maps.ask: What is the cheapest fix that makes the escalation boundary clear?
maps.when: The agent escalates easy cases and keeps going on hard ones, or someone proposes a new signal to route escalations on.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Guidance is vague; errors in both directions (easy cases escalated, hard ones kept)
Explicit criteria plus a few contrasting examples
Clarifies a fuzzy boundary cheaply and proportionately
Clear criteria and examples exist and still fail; there is a large labelled history and time to build and maintain a model
Heavier; proportionate only after the cheap fix and at that scale
Proposal: escalate on anger or sentiment
Customer explicitly asks for a person
An explicit demand is a trigger
Human receiving an escalation lacks context
Improves the handoff, not the decision
maps.rule: Fuzzy escalation boundaries get explicit criteria plus a few contrasting examples, not a new model. Self-rated confidence and sentiment don't measure complexity.

maps.for: Which customer record to act on
maps.ask: What is the source of truth for who this customer is?
maps.when: A customer's name matches account records and the agent must decide whose account to act on.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Chat arrives with a signed-in, verified account
Return all matches; ask for an order number or postcode
Refund attempted before identity is verified
Ranking or confidence used to pick a match
Replace with a question to the customer
maps.rule: Several matching records means ask the customer for an identifier. Do not choose by recency, score or ranking.

maps.for: Handling and reporting a subagent's failed or empty lookup
maps.ask: Did the lookup actually run, and should the subagent handle the error itself or hand it up?
maps.when: A subagent's search or lookup returns nothing, times out or errors, and the coordinator must decide what to do next.
head: What happened
Subagent should
Why
rows: Return a valid empty result; don't retry
Not an error; the coordinator can act on it
Retry locally with backoff, then report
Lookup failed and won't clear soon (timeout, outage)
Report a structured error: failure type, query tried, partial results, alternatives
The coordinator chooses the recovery: hold, escalate or retry later
The coordinator can fix and resend
Hides what was tried and what remains
maps.rule: Never let a failed lookup look like an empty one. Handle brief glitches locally; hand up longer failures with the failure type, the query, partial results and alternatives.

maps.for: What to do when a long session fills up or degrades
maps.ask: Is the session just full, or has it degraded, and what is flooding it?
maps.when: A long coding session is filling up, slowing down, or giving vague and contradictory answers.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Nearly full, answers still specific; only the gist is needed from here
Answers vague, “typical patterns”, contradictions; specifics still needed
Write findings to a scratchpad or notes file; a fresh session reads it
Repeated verbose output (logs, test runs) floods the context
Verbose work done in the main session
Delegate to a subagent that returns a summary
Exploring an unfamiliar codebase, lots of reading still to do
Coming back after files changed; earlier tool results are stale
New session from a structured summary
Progress must persist across a session boundary
Long job may crash or be interrupted mid-way
One long review thins out in the middle
maps.rule: If the session is healthy but full, use /compact. If it has degraded or the work crosses sessions, write the findings to a file and start a fresh session from it, and send noisy, repeated work to a subagent that returns only a summary.

maps.for: Carrying long work across a break, crash or handover
maps.ask: What carries the state forward: the conversation, a file on disk, or a fresh summary?
maps.when: Long work must be picked up after a pause or crash, or handed to another person or machine.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Findings needed across sessions or by another person
Crash or interruption in a long job, files changed since
State manifest or progress file, read on restart
The conversation is stale; restart from saved state
Same person, same machine, nothing or few changes since the pause
--resume the named session, plus a note of what changed
Resuming after edits you made yourself
Tell the agent which files changed
It is unaware of the changes
Earlier tool results largely stale, or the work moves machines
New session from a structured summary
Try two approaches from one starting point
Session long and full, but work continues now or ends today
Frees space in place, loses some detail
Big noisy search or verbose exploration
maps.rule: Keep progress for long work in a file on disk outside the chat, and start fresh from a summary when much has changed. A resumed conversation remembers what was said, not what is on disk now.

maps.for: Keeping noisy search output out of the main context
maps.ask: Is the noise predictable enough to exclude, or does it need filtering somewhere else?
maps.when: A codebase search returns far more output than you need.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Explore subagent filters in its own context
Context already flooded, work ends soon
maps.rule: Send noisy discovery to an Explore subagent that returns a short summary. Narrow the search instead only when the noise sits under predictable paths.

maps.for: Proving a category is ready to skip human review
maps.ask: Which number do you actually have, and does it cover the category you plan to automate?
maps.when: Someone wants to automate extraction or review because headline accuracy looks high.
head: Situation
Right step
Why
rows: High overall accuracy, but the target type is a small slice or rare in the sample
Stratified sample of that type (and by field); give rare, high-impact types a quota
Averages hide weak categories; too few samples to judge
Per-category figures exist for some categories
Type's accuracy is known; errors cluster on certain fields, or individual items must be routed
Field-level confidence calibrated on labelled data that covers every type
Routes only uncertain values to review
Don't route on it until it is calibrated on labelled data
Two runs or two independent extractors agree
Agreement shows repeatability, not correctness; double cost and no per-type rate
Use it for the overall number only
After launch, watching error rates in confident output over time
Stratified random sampling of high-confidence items
Use it as a consistency check
Enforces the rule; says nothing about quality
maps.rule: An overall score is not a per-category score. Before automating, measure each type you plan to automate with a stratified sample; calibrated field-level confidence comes after, for routing, and stratified sampling keeps watch after launch.

maps.for: Finding where a citation lost its source
maps.ask: At which stage did the claim lose the link to its source?
maps.when: A report's citations are missing, guessed or pointing to the wrong source.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Findings arrive as prose with sources named in passing; summaries have no document or page info
Structured fields (claim, URL, title, page), with content kept separate from metadata
Citations guessed after the prose is written; synthesis rewrites and drops the links
Emit claim-to-source mappings and pass them through as data
Links are carried, but a few are still wrong
Pipeline cannot change, and time is available
Verify each citation against its page
Two reputable sources disagree on one figure; one chosen silently
Show both, each with its source
Figures look contradictory but differ by date
maps.rule: Provenance is carried, not recovered: structure claim-to-source mappings where they start and keep them through every hand-off. Rebuilding attribution after the fact is guessing.

maps.ask: Is this a genuine conflict or a change over time, and what does the reader need?
maps.when: Two or more sources give different values for the same figure.
head: Situation
Right handling
Why
rows: Record publication and collection dates; compare like periods
A time difference is not a contradiction
Values carry effective dates that order them
Keep all with dates; the current value is the latest effective one
A sequence (a history), not a contradiction
Same period, both reputable, still differ (two values in force at once)
Show both, each with source, date and method, in a structured section; note the conflict and let a human decide
The system itself must resolve a gap in evidence
Re-delegate a targeted search, then re-synthesise
Fills gaps when resolution is the system's job
A figure cannot be found in its source
Claims lose their sources in summaries
Reviewers have limited time and need to focus it
Calibrated confidence routes weak claims to review
Mixed content types (financial data vs news)
Render financial data as tables, news as prose
maps.rule: Check the dates before calling it a contradiction. When good sources genuinely disagree, show both with their sources and dates and let the reader judge; don't pick a winner.

maps.for: Speeding up human review of extracted values
maps.ask: Where is the reviewers' time going, and what would save it?
maps.when: People checking extracted values are slow.
head: Where time goes
What helps
Mechanism
rows: Finding where each value came from
Reconstructing why a value was chosen
Keep both with source and date
maps.rule: When people verify extracted values, give each value its source: the page and the exact text.
